title_en: Hubei Jinhua Industrial Co., Ltd. v. Su Jinshui et al. — dispute over commercial housing sales contract
ruling_gist_en: 1. When a people's court retries a case upon a procuratorate's protest, the scope of retrial shall generally be limited to the scope of the original trial. A party's litigation claims are different from the reasons and grounds supporting the claims. If the reasons and grounds for a party's claims differ from those raised by the procuratorate in its protest, it does not mean that the party's request for protest has not been supported by the procuratorate. If a party's retrial request does not exceed the scope of the original trial, the people's court shall hear it in the retrial.

full_text_en:
Hubei Jinhua Industrial Co., Ltd. v. Su Jinshui et al.

— Dispute over Commercial Housing Sale Contract

【Ruling Summary】

I. In a retrial case initiated by the procuratorial authority's protest, the scope of the retrial generally should be limited to the scope of the original trial. A party's claims are different from the reasons and basis supporting such claims. Where the reasons and basis for a party's claims are different from those raised in the procuratorial authority's protest, it does not mean that the party's request for a protest has not been supported by the procuratorial authority. Where the party's claims in the retrial do not exceed the scope of the original trial, the people's court shall hear them in the retrial.

II. In circumstances where a real estate development enterprise entrusts an agency to sell housing, the real estate development enterprise's failure to be informed by the entrusted agency that a particular property has already been sold, resulting in a double sale of the same property, constitutes a business risk arising from its selection and supervision of the entrusted agent. This risk may not be shifted onto the home buyer. Where the real estate development enterprise on this ground requests that the punitive damages provided for in Article 8 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Contracts for the Sale of Commercial Housing be exempted, the people's court shall not support such request.

Supreme People's Court Civil Judgment

(2012) Min Kang Zi No. 24

Protesting Authority: Supreme People's Procuratorate of the People's Republic of China

Petitioner (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Hubei Jinhua Industrial Co., Ltd., domiciled at Top Floor, Jinhua Tower, No. 625 Jianshe Avenue, Jianghan District, Wuhan City, Hubei Province

Legal Representative: Li Xizhi, Chairman of the Board

Agent ad litem: Wang Weiqiao, Lawyer, Hubei Chenfeng Law Firm

Agent ad litem: Han Yi, Employee of the Company

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Su Jinshui, male, born October 1, 1977, Han ethnicity, domiciled at Room 1, 12th Floor, Building 27-3, Yongqing Road, Jiang'an District, Wuhan City, Hubei Province

Agent ad litem: Liu Dengpan, Lawyer, Hubei Shanhe Law Firm

Agent ad litem: Chen Bin, male, born December 12, 1942, Han ethnicity, domiciled at Room 2, 7th Floor, No. 15 Beihu West Road, Jianghan District, Wuhan City, Hubei Province

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Wuhan Hao Yu Real Estate Consulting Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 105 Gaoxiong Road, Jiang'an District, Wuhan City, Hubei Province

Legal Representative: Yao Fuyao, Chairman of the Board

Agent ad litem: Luo Jian, Lawyer, Hubei Shanhe Law Firm

In the case of dispute over commercial housing sale contract between Hubei Jinhua Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jinhua Company) and Su Jinshui, Wuhan Hao Yu Real Estate Consulting Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hao Yu Company), Jinhua Company, dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2009) E Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 28 rendered by the Hubei High People's Court, filed a petition with the procuratorial authority. The Supreme People's Procuratorate filed a protest with this Court by Civil Protest Letter (2011) Gao Jian Min Kang No. 83. This Court, by Civil Ruling (2012) Min Kang Zi No. 24 dated March 19, 2012, decided to bring the case up for retrial. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel and held a public hearing of the case. The Supreme People's Procuratorate designated Procurator Wang Tianying and Clerk Wang Liuyu to appear in court. Agent ad litem of Jinhua Company Wang Weiqiao and Han Yi, agent ad litem of Su Jinshui Liu Dengpan and Chen Bin, and agent ad litem of Hao Yu Company Luo Jian appeared in court. The case is now concluded.

Upon retrial, this Court finds the following facts:

On March 12, 2005, Jinhua Company and Hao Yu Company signed a "Chutian Constellation" Commercial Housing Minimum Guaranteed Floor Price and Full Responsibility Sales Contract. In June of the same year, the parties signed a Supplemental Agreement on Sales Agency. On March 28, 2006, the parties signed a Supplemental Agreement to the "Chutian Constellation" Commercial Housing Minimum Guaranteed Floor Price and Full Responsibility Sales Contract. The "Chutian Constellation" Commercial Housing Minimum Guaranteed Floor Price and Full Responsibility Sales Contract stipulated: Hao Yu Company would act as the sales agent for the "Chutian Constellation" project developed by Jinhua Company, located at the intersection of Qingnian Road and Wansongyuan Horizontal Road, Jianghan District, Wuhan City, with a total commercial housing gross floor area of approximately 50,000 square meters; except for two floors of residential housing and 700 square meters of shops, the remainder of the commercial housing floor area commissioned by Jinhua Company to Hao Yu Company for agency sales fell within the scope of the agency; all externally sold floor areas, after being stamped with the signature and seal of Jinhua Company, were to be handed over to Hao Yu Company for external sales, with specific unit types and floor areas attached as an appendix to this contract; to ensure the normal conduct of sales work, Jinhua Company was to designate a sales manager to liaise and coordinate with Hao Yu Company's sales work, and designate financial personnel to receive payment from customers and issue valid receipts; the "Commercial Housing Sale Contract" and related documents for this project required the affixing of Jinhua Company's company seal to become effective; any contracts or documents signed by any other unit or individual were invalid. The Supplemental Agreement to the "'Chutian Constellation' Commercial Housing Minimum Guaranteed Floor Price and Full Responsibility Sales Contract" stipulated: April 2006 was to be a planning month for promoting and marketing this building, during which sales would be suspended for one month.

In April 2006, Su Jinshui and Jinhua Company signed two "'Chutian Constellation' Commercial Housing Subscription Contracts" for the purchase of Shop Nos. 06 and 07. Both subscription contracts indicated Party A (Seller) as Jinhua Company and Party B (Buyer) as Su Jinshui, and each was affixed with the "Special Seal for 'Chutian Constellation' Sales Contract of Hubei Jinhua Industrial Co., Ltd.". Both subscription contracts also indicated the sales office address as the intersection of Qingnian Road and Wansongyuan Horizontal Road and the subscribed unit numbers as Shop Nos. 06 and 07, respectively. In the same month, Su Jinshui signed two "Wuhan Commercial Housing Sale Contracts" with the sales personnel of Hao Yu Company, Jinhua Company's house sales agent. The first contract stipulated: Seller as Jinhua Company, Entrusted Agency as Hao Yu Company, Buyer as Su Jinshui; the commercial housing purchased by the Buyer was Shop No. 06 on the first floor; gross floor area was 145.39 square meters, price was RMB 30,476.72 per square meter, totaling RMB 4,431,010; the contract was to be held in one copy each by the Seller, Buyer, property department, and bank. On the Seller's signature/seal page of this contract, the "Special Seal for 'Chutian Constellation' Sales Contract of Hubei Jinhua Industrial Co., Ltd." was affixed, and on the Buyer's signature/seal page, Su Jinshui signed. This contract had multiple corrections and the attached floor plan lacked continuous seals along the edge. The second contract stipulated the same parties as above, and the commercial housing purchased by the Buyer was Shop No. 07 on the first floor; gross floor area was 64.40 square meters, price was RMB 33,385.09 per square meter, totaling RMB 2,150,000; the contract was to be held in one copy each by the Seller, Buyer, and property department. On the Entrusted Agency's signature/seal page of this contract, the "Special Seal for Sales Contract of Wuhan Hao Yu Real Estate Consulting Co., Ltd." was affixed, and on the Buyer's signature/seal page, Su Jinshui signed. Jinhua Company did not affix its seal on the Seller's signature/seal page of this contract. Except for RMB 20,000 paid in cash, Su Jinshui paid the purchase price for the housing in five installments on April 11 and April 30, 2006, totaling RMB 4,211,010, through a POS machine installed by Hao Yu Company with approval at "Chutian Constellation", and on May 17, 2006, paid RMB 1,400,000 by bank transfer. Hao Yu Company issued three receipts to Su Jinshui on April 11, April 30, and May 17, 2006, for RMB 2,000,000, RMB 2,231,010, and RMB 1,400,000 respectively, totaling RMB 5,631,010. Among these, the receipt for RMB 2,000,000 issued by Hao Yu Company indicated it was a deposit, consistent with the total deposit amount recorded in the two subscription contracts.

On June 20, 2006, Hao Yu Company sent a Notice of Termination of the "'Chutian Constellation' Commercial Housing Minimum Guaranteed Floor Price and Full Responsibility Sales Contract" to Jinhua Company, stating that because Jinhua Company had provided real estate without legal sale qualifications and could not pay the decoration fees as agreed, the purpose of the contract could not be achieved, and therefore notified the termination of the contract. Thereafter, the sales personnel of Hao Yu Company withdrew from the sales office and on July 30, 2006, completed the removal procedures for the POS machine installed at "Chutian Constellation". Jinhua Company reorganized its personnel to continue selling the project. After Hao Yu Company sent the notice of contract termination to Jinhua Company, it still retained originals of some housing sale contracts and other materials. The Wuhan Intermediate People's Court of Hubei Province organized a handover of these materials between the two parties on August 29, 2006. On September 29, 2006, Jinhua Company sold the Shop No. 07, which is the subject of this dispute, to Li Jing, and the commercial housing sale contract was filed with the Wuhan Real Estate Administration Bureau on September 30, 2006. On October 31, 2006, when Su Jinshui went to the "Chutian Constellation" sales office to request completion of the housing delivery procedures, Jinhua Company refused to complete the procedures on the grounds that the company had not signed a contract with him and had not received his payment for the housing, thus giving rise to this dispute. Su Jinshui applied for arbitration to the Wuhan Arbitration Commission on November 14, 2006. On January 16, 2007, Jinhua Company sold Shop No. 06, which is the subject of this dispute, to Li Shaowei, and the commercial housing sale contract was filed with the Wuhan Real Estate Administration Bureau on January 17, 2007. On July 16, 2007, the Wuhan Arbitration Commission rendered an award (2006) Wu Zhong Cai Zi No. 00858. On September 20, 2007, Jinhua Company applied to the Wuhan Intermediate People's Court of Hubei Province for revocation of this award. On January 11, 2008, the Wuhan Intermediate People's Court of Hubei Province revoked the award by Civil Ruling (2007) Wu Zhong Jian Zi No. 369. On April 7, 2008, Su Jinshui filed this lawsuit with the Wuhan Intermediate People's Court of Hubei Province, requesting a judgment: 1. confirming that the "Wuhan Commercial Housing Sale Contracts" signed by Su Jinshui and Jinhua Company for Shop Nos. 06 and 07 of "Chutian Constellation" were valid; 2. ordering that due to Jinhua Company's conduct rendering the purpose of the contracts unattainable, the "Wuhan Commercial Housing Sale Contracts" signed by Su Jinshui and Jinhua Company for Shop Nos. 06 and 07 of "Chutian Constellation" be terminated; 3. ordering Jinhua Company to return Su Jinshui's payment of RMB 5,631,010 for the housing and compensate for interest losses of RMB 689,235; 4. ordering Jinhua Company to pay Su Jinshui damages of RMB 5,631,010 and arbitration fees of RMB 107,240; 5. ordering Hao Yu Company to bear joint and several liability for the claim set out in Item 3 above; 6. ordering Jinhua Company and Hao Yu Company to bear all litigation costs and property preservation costs of this case.

At first instance, the Wuhan Intermediate People's Court of Hubei Province held:

I. Regarding the validity and fault liability determination for Su Jinshui's submitted "Wuhan Commercial Housing Sale Contract" for Shop No. 06 (hereinafter referred to as the Contract No. 06). Although this contract was negotiated and signed between Hao Yu Company and Su Jinshui, given that only the seals of Su Jinshui and Jinhua Company appear on the contract, without the seal of Hao Yu Company as the entrusted agency, the parties to this contract can only be determined as Su Jinshui and Jinhua Company, and the agreed terms are binding only on them. Hao Yu Company does not enjoy any rights or assume any obligations under this contract. Although this contract exists only as a single original held by Su Jinshui, and the original contract contains multiple corrections and lacks continuous seals on the attached floor plan, these anomalies are insufficient to prove that the contract was forged by another party. Therefore, the content agreed in this contract represents the true intention of the parties, and the form and content of the contract do not violate legal provisions. This contract should be deemed valid. After the contract was signed, the home buyer should have paid the purchase price to the property developer in a timely manner in accordance with the terms of the contract. However, Su Jinshui did not pay the price to Jinhua Company in accordance with the principle of privity of contract but instead paid the purchase price to Hao Yu Company and had it issue the receipt, ultimately resulting in Hao Yu Company's unjust enrichment by taking possession of the price. Thus, since Su Jinshui's payment of the purchase price failed to be delivered to Jinhua Company as agreed, rendering the purpose of the contract unattainable, the contract should be rescinded, and the fault lies with the buyer Su Jinshui himself. Jinhua Company, as the seller, bears no fault in this regard.

II. Regarding the validity and fault liability determination for the "Wuhan Commercial Housing Sale Contract" for Shop No. 07 (hereinafter referred to as the Contract No. 07). Since only the seals of Su Jinshui and the entrusted agency Hao Yu Company appear on the signature/seal page of this contract, without the seal of Jinhua Company, in accordance with Article 16(1) of the Measures for the Administration of Commercial Housing Sales (Ministry of Construction Order No. 88, issued on April 4, 2001), this contract does not have the effect of a commercial housing sale contract. Even if Su Jinshui, as a home buyer, was not aware of the relevant laws and regulations when signing this contract, he should, as a matter of common sense, have understood the basic transaction knowledge that a housing sale contract must be signed by the property developer, and he should not have relied on this contract to directly pay the purchase price to Hao Yu Company. Therefore, this housing purchase transaction between Su Jinshui and Hao Yu Company was unrelated to Jinhua Company, and Jinhua Company bears no fault in this regard.

In summary, Su Jinshui's payment of RMB 5,631,010 in total to Hao Yu Company was entirely due to Su Jinshui's own fault, and the liability does not lie with Jinhua Company. Since Hao Yu Company improperly received Su Jinshui's payment for the housing, according to Article 92 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, Hao Yu Company must return the payment it received from Su Jinshui. The court at first instance supported Su Jinshui's claim requesting Hao Yu Company to bear joint and several liability for returning the purchase price of RMB 5,631,010 and compensating for the loss of use of the funds. Su Jinshui's claim for rescission of the Contract No. 06, given that both parties can no longer continue performance of the contract, was confirmed by the court at first instance. Su Jinshui argued that his signing of the purchase contract and payment of the price was based on Hao Yu Company's authorized agency, and that the internal agreement between the agent and the principal does not bind the buyer. The substance of this argument was to request the court to find that Hao Yu Company's conduct in this case constituted apparent agency, thereby requiring Jinhua Company to bear the liability for returning the purchase price of RMB 5,631,010 and compensating for corresponding losses. The collegial panel opined that whether Hao Yu Company's conduct in this case constituted apparent agency should be determined in accordance with Article 49 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China. Although the Contract No. 06 signed by Su Jinshui was made by Hao Yu Company in the name of the principal, Hao Yu Company was not a counterparty to the contract, and Su Jinshui had no reason to pay the purchase price for Shop No. 06 to a party who was not the counterparty to the contract. As for the Contract No. 07 signed by Su Jinshui, Hao Yu Company did not sign the contract in the name of the principal, and Su Jinshui did not pay the purchase price for Shop No. 07 to the principal. Therefore, Hao Yu Company's conduct in this case did not constitute apparent agency. Consequently, Su Jinshui's claim on this ground that Jinhua Company should bear the liability for returning the purchase price of RMB 5,631,010 and compensating for corresponding losses was not supported. Accordingly, the Wuhan Intermediate People's Court of Hubei Province rendered Civil Judgment (2008) Wu Min Chu Zi No. 56 on December 2, 2008: 1. rescinded the "Wuhan Commercial Housing Sale Contract" for Shop No. 06 signed between Su Jinshui and Jinhua Company; 2. ordered Hao Yu Company, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, to return to Su Jinshui the purchase price of RMB 5,631,010 and compensate for the loss of use of such funds (calculated based on the purchase price from May 1, 2006 to April 7, 2008, at the loan interest rate for the corresponding period set by the People's Bank of China); 3. dismissed Su Jinshui's other claims. Court costs of RMB 94,151 were to be borne by Su Jinshui in the amount of RMB 45,192.48 and by Hao Yu Company in the amount of RMB 48,958.52. Pre-litigation property preservation costs of RMB 5,000 were to be borne by Hao Yu Company.

Su Jinshui, dissatisfied with the above first-instance judgment, appealed to the Hubei High People's Court.

The High People's Court of Hubei Province held in the second instance that: 1. According to the "Chutian Constellation" Commercial Housing Minimum Guarantee and Lump-Sum Sales Contract, the Supplemental Agreement on Sales Agency, and the Supplemental Agreement to the "Chutian Constellation" Commercial Housing Minimum Guarantee and Lump-Sum Sales Contract signed between Jinhua Company and Haoyu Company, Haoyu Company acted as an agent for the sale of Jinhua Company's "Chutian Constellation" properties. A principal-agent relationship existed between Jinhua Company and Haoyu Company, with Jinhua Company as the principal and Haoyu Company as the agent. Haoyu Company sold the first-floor shops Nos. 06 and 07 of "Chutian Constellation" to Su Jinshui. Su Jinshui and the sales staff of Haoyu Company signed two copies of the Wuhan Commercial Housing Sales Contract. Su Jinshui should be considered a third party. 2. Regarding the validity of Contract No. 06. The contract explicitly named Jinhua Company as the seller, Haoyu Company as the authorized agency, and Su Jinshui as the buyer. Although Haoyu Company did not affix its seal to the contract, Jinhua Company did affix its official seal, and Su Jinshui also signed the contract, so the contract is valid. Since Su Jinshui had been negotiating the purchase of Shop No. 06 solely with Haoyu Company, and Contract No. 06 clearly designated Haoyu Company as the authorized agency, Haoyu Company's failure to affix its seal does not affect its status as the agent. Because Haoyu Company did not present to Su Jinshui the "Chutian Constellation" Commercial Housing Minimum Guarantee and Lump-Sum Sales Contract it had signed with Jinhua Company, Su Jinshui was unaware that Haoyu Company had no authority to collect the purchase price. Furthermore, the Wuhan Commercial Housing Sales Contract contained no provision on this matter, and Jinhua Company had not communicated this limitation to Su Jinshui. Therefore, Su Jinshui's payment of the purchase price to Haoyu Company was not improper. According to Article 65, Paragraph 3 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC, which provides that "where the power of attorney is not clearly specified, the principal shall bear civil liability towards the third party, and the agent shall bear joint liability," Su Jinshui's payment should be deemed as payment to Jinhua Company. The first instance court's finding that Su Jinshui's payment could not be delivered to Jinhua Company as agreed, thereby frustrating the purpose of the contract and warranting rescission, lacked factual and legal basis and is corrected. 3. Regarding the validity of Contract No. 07. Although Jinhua Company did not affix its seal to the contract, and only Haoyu Company's seal appeared, the contract explicitly named Jinhua Company as the seller, Haoyu Company as the authorized agency, and Su Jinshui as the buyer. Moreover, based on the process of signing Contract No. 06, Su Jinshui was aware that Haoyu Company, as the agent, had authority to sell the "Chutian Constellation" properties on behalf of Jinhua Company. According to Article 402 of the Contract Law of the PRC, which provides that "where the agent concludes a contract in its own name within the scope of the principal's authorization with a third party who, at the time of concluding the contract, is aware of the agency relationship between the agent and the principal, the contract shall directly bind the principal and the third party, unless there is conclusive evidence that the contract only binds the agent and the third party," Contract No. 07 directly binds Jinhua Company and Su Jinshui, and the contract is valid. The first instance court's finding that Su Jinshui's purchase of Shop No. 07 from Haoyu Company was unrelated to Jinhua Company lacked factual and legal basis. Since Su Jinshui was unaware that Haoyu Company had no authority to collect the purchase price, his payment to Haoyu Company was not improper and should be deemed as payment to Jinhua Company. As for Haoyu Company's receipt of the purchase price of RMB 5,631,010 specified in the two Wuhan Commercial Housing Sales Contracts from Su Jinshui without delivering it to Jinhua Company, this constitutes a separate legal relationship, and Jinhua Company may pursue its rights separately. 4. After the delivery of the two commercial housing sales contracts, Su Jinshui paid the purchase price of RMB 5,631,010 to Jinhua Company as agreed, fulfilling his contractual obligations. However, Jinhua Company unilaterally resold Shops Nos. 06 and 07, which had been sold to Su Jinshui, to others, constituting a breach of contract and rendering further performance impossible. Su Jinshui's request to rescind the two Wuhan Commercial Housing Sales Contracts is supported by the relevant provisions of the Contract Law of the PRC. According to Article 8, Paragraph 2 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Commercial Housing Sales Contracts, Jinhua Company must return the purchase price of RMB 5,631,010 to Su Jinshui and compensate for interest losses during the period of fund occupation. However, since all payments made by Su Jinshui were received by Haoyu Company, and Jinhua Company received no funds, and after the first instance court ordered Haoyu Company to return the purchase price and compensate for interest losses, Haoyu Company did not appeal the first instance judgment, which should be deemed as acceptance. Therefore, this aspect is not modified. Jinhua Company shall bear supplementary compensation liability for the portion Haoyu Company is unable to repay. Pursuant to the above judicial interpretation, Su Jinshui is entitled to claim compensation from Jinhua Company up to the amount of the purchase price paid. However, considering that Su Jinshui's original contract contained numerous alterations and the attached floor plan lacked a continuous seal, and that Contract No. 07 bore only Haoyu Company's seal without Jinhua Company's seal, Su Jinshui was negligent in his review, contributing to the occurrence of this dispute. The court, in its discretion, orders Jinhua Company to pay Su Jinshui compensation of 50% of the purchase price, amounting to RMB 2,815,505. The remaining liability shall be borne by Su Jinshui. Su Jinshui's claim for arbitration fees, being litigation costs necessarily incurred, is not supported. In summary, Su Jinshui's relevant appeal claims are upheld, while other claims lacking factual and legal basis are dismissed. The first instance court's factual findings were generally correct, but the application of law was erroneous. Accordingly, on December 23, 2009, the High People's Court of Hubei Province rendered Civil Judgment (2009) E Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 28: 1. Affirm Item 2 of the main text of Civil Judgment (2008) Wu Min Chu Zi No. 56 of the Wuhan Intermediate People's Court; 2. Reverse Items 1 and 3 of the main text of Civil Judgment (2008) Wu Min Chu Zi No. 56 of the Wuhan Intermediate People's Court; 3. Rescind the Wuhan Commercial Housing Sales Contracts for Shops Nos. 06 and 07 signed between Su Jinshui and Hubei Jinhua Industrial Co., Ltd.; 4. Hubei Jinhua Industrial Co., Ltd. shall bear supplementary compensation liability for the payment obligations of Wuhan Haoyu Real Estate Consulting Co., Ltd.; 5. Hubei Jinhua Industrial Co., Ltd. shall pay Su Jinshui RMB 2,815,505 within ten days of the effective date of this judgment; 6. Dismiss Su Jinshui's other claims. Litigation costs for the first instance shall be borne as determined in the first instance judgment. Litigation costs for the second instance, amounting to RMB 94,151, shall be borne by Su Jinshui in the amount of RMB 28,245.30 and by Hubei Jinhua Industrial Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 65,905.70.

Jinhua Company, dissatisfied with the above second instance judgment, filed a petition with the procuratorial authority.

The Supreme People's Procuratorate filed a protest with this Court, asserting that the above second instance judgment erroneously applied the law. 1. Article 8, Paragraph 2 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Commercial Housing Sales Contracts provides that where the seller resells the property to a third party after the contract is concluded, the buyer may claim compensation from the seller not exceeding the full amount of the purchase price paid. This provision, as a punitive damages rule, aims to sanction and deter fraudulent and malicious breach of contract that abandons the principle of good faith and seriously undermines the security of market transactions. Therefore, its application requires the seller to have malicious intent to breach the contract. 2. Based on the facts established at trial: Haoyu Company did not inform Jinhua Company of the sale of the two shops in question. When Jinhua Company sold Shop No. 07 on September 30, 2006, Su Jinshui had not yet demanded delivery of the property, and the dispute over that property had not entered arbitration or litigation proceedings. In other words, Jinhua Company resold Shop No. 07 without knowledge that it had already been sold. Moreover, Contract No. 07 lacked the seal of Jinhua Company as the seller, bearing only the seal of Haoyu Company as the authorized agency. Jinhua Company did not have the subjective intent of "selling one property to multiple buyers" as required by Article 8, Paragraph 2 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation, nor did it have the fraudulent intent to conceal the truth. Jinhua Company's sale of Shop No. 06 occurred on January 16, 2007, after Su Jinshui had demanded delivery and the dispute over the property had entered arbitration. In other words, Jinhua Company resold Shop No. 06 with full knowledge of the existing dispute, demonstrating clear intent, and its conduct was the fundamental cause of the "selling one property to two buyers" situation regarding Shop No. 06. Thus, the underlying reasons for the frustration of purpose under Contracts No. 06 and No. 07 differ, and the legal bases for their application also differ. The second instance judgment's application of Article 8, Paragraph 2 of the said Interpretation to order Jinhua Company to pay Su Jinshui punitive damages of 50% of the purchase price for Shops Nos. 06 and 07, amounting to RMB 2,815,505, was erroneous in law. 3. The second instance judgment's order to rescind Contracts No. 06 and No. 07 between Su Jinshui and Jinhua Company was erroneous. Contract No. 06 bore Jinhua Company's special seal for sales contracts, while Contract No. 07 lacked Jinhua Company's seal as the seller, bearing only Haoyu Company's seal as the authorized agency. Therefore, Haoyu Company's sale of Shop No. 07 was unrelated to Jinhua Company. Furthermore, the purchase price of RMB 5,631,010 paid by Su Jinshui to Haoyu Company was not delivered to Jinhua Company. Jinhua Company resold Shop No. 07 to another party without any knowledge, and thus had no bad faith. Therefore, there was no basis for rescinding the contract for Shop No. 07. The second instance judgment's order to rescind Contract No. 07 between Su Jinshui and Jinhua Company was erroneous. Similarly, Jinhua Company's supplementary compensation liability for Haoyu Company's repayment of the purchase price of RMB 5.63 million to Su Jinshui should not include the purchase price for Shop No. 07.

Jinhua Company agreed with the protest opinion and argued that: 1. Haoyu Company had no authority to sell Shops Nos. 06 and 07 of "Chutian Constellation." Haoyu Company exceeded the scope of agency under their contract and sold these shops during the suspension period of the project. This was an ultra vires act that did not bind Jinhua Company, and Haoyu Company should bear the liability. 2. Su Jinshui was seriously at fault in the purchase, and the situation did not meet the legal requirements for apparent authority. The advertising campaign was launched on May 1, 2006, but Su Jinshui signed the contract with Haoyu Company in April 2006. Su Jinshui failed to properly review the obviously defective purchase contracts. Contracts No. 06 and No. 07 differed in version, the seals on the two contracts were different, the content differed, Contract No. 06 had multiple alterations and pasted marks, the payment receipts were issued by Haoyu Company rather than Jinhua Company, and part of Su Jinshui's payment was made to an individual, Zeng Qingting. 3. In this case, Haoyu Company exceeded its authority in selling Shops Nos. 06 and 07, and Jinhua Company was not at fault. The situation did not meet the legal requirements for apparent authority. Jinhua Company's resale of Shops Nos. 06 and 07 did not constitute a breach of contract, and Jinhua Company should not bear supplementary liability for Haoyu Company's repayment of the purchase price to Su Jinshui, nor should it bear compensation of 50% of the purchase price to Su Jinshui. Jinhua Company requested the reversal of Civil Judgment (2009) E Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 28 of the High People's Court of Hubei Province, a finding that Contracts No. 06 and No. 07 were invalid, and dismissal of Su Jinshui's claims for return of the purchase price, interest loss compensation, compensation of RMB 5,631,010, and arbitration fees. It also requested that all litigation costs and property preservation fees for the first and second instances be borne by Su Jinshui.

Su Jinshui argued in defense that: 1. The protest opinion considered the two purchase contracts to be valid, while Jinhua Company argued they were invalid. According to Article 33 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC in the Retrial Procedure, the scope of review in a protest retrial must be limited to the scope of the protester's support for the party's claims. Since the protest did not support Jinhua Company's petition, the retrial proceedings should be terminated at this point (referring to the court hearing), and Jinhua Company's views should not be included in the scope of review. 2. The existing protest grounds of the procuratorial authority violate the fundamental principles of the civil agency system, sacrifice the security of transactions, and cause significant damage to the good faith environment in civil transactions. Haoyu Company was an authorized sales agent of Jinhua Company and had the authority to sell the properties in question. This case involves agency sales, not apparent authority. The contracts directly bind the seller of the shops. Regarding Shop No. 07, the first page of the purchase contract clearly identified Jinhua Company as the seller and Haoyu Company as the agent. Haoyu Company affixed its seal in the agent signature section on the last page. This is an agency sale where the agent disclosed the principal. The protest opinion's view that the contract is unrelated to Jinhua Company simply because only Haoyu Company's seal appears on the last page seriously misunderstands the agency system. Whether or not Jinhua Company was actually aware, Haoyu Company's acts represent Jinhua Company. In civil legal relations, Jinhua Company must be deemed to have known. Thus, after the property had already been sold, Jinhua Company's resale frustrated Su Jinshui's contractual purpose, and Jinhua Company should bear double compensation liability. The second instance judgment's order for Jinhua Company to bear only supplementary compensation for the purchase price and 50% of the breach compensation was already lenient. 3. The Wuhan Intermediate People's Court's actions in setting aside the arbitration award, the first instance judgment, and the enforcement were all illegal. 4. Jinhua Company is evading liability, and its arguments lack legal basis. This case only requires determining whether an agency relationship existed. Jinhua Company argued that the contract was invalid due to alterations, but the power of attorney and law firm letter submitted by Jinhua Company to the first instance court also had obvious alterations. Su Jinshui, as a buyer, has not had his funds returned for over six years, and the property was resold. Haoyu Company and Jinhua Company have suffered no loss and have not actually borne any liability. Jinhua Company is using litigation to shift its own liability for poor partner selection. 5. This case should find that Jinhua Company breached the two sales contracts by selling the property to another buyer, frustrating the contractual purpose, and Jinhua Company should be ordered to bear double compensation for the full amount. However, Su Jinshui respects the second instance judgment. He requests the dismissal of Jinhua Company's petition on the grounds that Jinhua Company did not agree with the protest opinion.

Haoyu Company argued in defense that: 1. As the sales agent for Jinhua Company's property, Haoyu Company's acts should bind Jinhua Company. In this case, as the exclusive sales agent for Jinhua Company's "Chutian Constellation" property, Haoyu Company's agency authority is beyond doubt. Whether Jinhua Company was aware of Haoyu Company's acts and whether Haoyu Company delivered Su Jinshui's payments to Jinhua Company do not constitute grounds for invalidating the agency. Haoyu Company's breach of the Minimum Guarantee and Lump-Sum Sales Contract cannot be asserted against a third party outside that contract. The Wuhan Commercial Housing Sales Contracts signed by Su Jinshui to purchase the "Chutian Constellation" shops developed by Jinhua Company are lawful and valid. All legal consequences arising therefrom shall, under the Contract Law and General Principles of the Civil Law, be borne by Jinhua Company, the principal. Haoyu Company acknowledges that its interception of Su Jinshui's purchase price was improper and led to this dispute. However, Haoyu Company's conduct was a desperate measure following Jinhua Company's unreasoned refusal to pay agency commissions and premium sharing. In effect, Haoyu Company improperly sought self-help, shifting its own business risk to Su Jinshui. For this reason, Haoyu Company has repeatedly agreed to assign its claim of nearly RMB 8 million against Jinhua Company to Su Jinshui to compensate for the losses caused by its own actions. 2. The second instance judgment's finding that Jinhua Company is liable for compensation for "selling one property to two buyers" was factually sound and legally correct. The judicial interpretation on commercial housing sales does not require a finding of subjective intent for "selling one property to two buyers." Whether or not Jinhua Company actually knew that Su Jinshui had signed the Wuhan Commercial Housing Sales Contracts, Haoyu Company's acts represent Jinhua Company. In civil legal fact, Jinhua Company must be deemed to have known. Therefore, Jinhua Company's resale of the disputed shops after they had already been sold frustrated the purpose of the Wuhan Commercial Housing Sales Contracts signed by Su Jinshui, and Jinhua Company must bear compensation liability not exceeding double the purchase price. Haoyu Company requests that the second instance judgment be upheld.

This Court finds upon retrial: Regarding the first instance's finding that the lump-sum sales contract and supplemental agreements signed between Jinhua Company and Haoyu Company were lawful and valid, since Jinhua Company and Haoyu Company have no dispute on this point, and the procuratorial authority did not protest this aspect, and the above contracts do not violate mandatory legal provisions, this Court confirms it. Based on the protest of the procuratorial authority and the parties' arguments, the main issues in this case can be summarized as follows: First, whether the legal consequences of Haoyu Company's sale of Shops Nos. 06 and 07 to Su Jinshui should be attributed to Jinhua Company; Second, whether Jinhua Company should bear corresponding compensation liability to Su Jinshui for the resale of Shops Nos. 06 and 07.

I. Regarding whether the legal consequences of Haoyu Company's sale of Shops Nos. 06 and 07 to Su Jinshui should be attributed to Jinhua Company.

According to the provisions of Article 63 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC, a principal shall bear civil liability for an agency act performed by an agent in the principal's name within the scope of the agency authority. Therefore, in this case, whether the legal consequences of Hao Yu Company's sales conduct are attributable to Jinan Company depends on whether Hao Yu Company's sales conduct constituted authorized agency. This Court finds that Hao Yu Company's sales conduct has constituted authorized agency for the following reasons: First, at the time of selling the involved properties, Jinan Company had granted Hao Yu Company exclusive full-course agency authority. Article 2 of the "Chutian Constellation" Commercial Housing Guaranteed Minimum Sales Contract signed between Jinan Company and Hao Yu Company stipulates, "Party A (referring to Jinan Company) authorizes Party B (referring to Hao Yu Company) as the exclusive full-course sales agent for this project, with the scope of agency including project marketing planning, sales agency, advertising, etc. Unless this contract expires or is terminated, or as otherwise defined by Party A in the early stage, Party A shall not sell the properties itself, or entrust other companies or individuals to sell." This clause clearly grants Hao Yu Company the agency authority to sell the involved properties, and the relevant newspaper advertisements and promotional materials also indicate Hao Yu Company's legal status as the "full-course marketing" agent for the property. Second, Hao Yu Company sold the involved shops in the name of Jinan Company, not in its own name. The headings of both Contract No. 06 and Contract No. 07 list the seller as Jinan Company and clearly identify Hao Yu Company as Jinan Company's entrusted agency. Third, the signatures of Su Jinshui appear at the end of both Contract No. 06 and Contract No. 07. Contract No. 06 bears the seal of the sales contract of the seller, Jinan Company, and Contract No. 07 bears the sales contract seal affixed by Hao Yu Company as the entrusted agent of Jinan Company. Fourth, during the process of purchasing the shops, Su Jinshui also obtained the "Chutian Constellation" Commercial Housing Subscription Contracts for Shop No. 06 and Shop No. 07, both of which bear the sales contract seal of Jinan Company. Fifth, Su Jinshui signed Contract No. 06 and Contract No. 07 on-site at the property sales office and paid the majority of the purchase price via an on-site POS terminal. It is evident that Hao Yu Company's conduct of selling the involved shops to Su Jinshui in the name of Jinan Company is sufficient to be deemed as authorized agency, and Su Jinshui, as an ordinary home buyer, had ample reason to believe that Hao Yu Company had the agency authority to sell the involved shops. In addition, although some property promotional materials contain the phrase "enthusiastically launched on May 1, 2006," such phrasing does not include a public declaration prohibiting Hao Yu Company from selling the involved shops before May 1, 2006. At the same time, several agreements made between Jinan Company and Hao Yu Company regarding the closure period, collection authority, and seal authority are internal agreements between them, which were not publicly disclosed and cannot be asserted against a bona fide home buyer. Jinan Company argued in retrial that Shop No. 06 and Shop No. 07 were not within the scope of authority granted to Hao Yu Company, but Hao Yu Company denied this, and Jinan Company failed to provide evidence to prove it. Therefore, this Court does not support Jinan Company's claim that Hao Yu Company's sale of the involved shops was an ultra vires act and not binding on Jinan Company. As for Jinan Company's argument that Su Jinshui had serious fault in the purchase due to his failure to notice that the property advertising was "enthusiastically launched" on May 1, 2006, his failure to conduct necessary review of the contract version, alterations, seals, and receipt issuers, and the fact that some of Su Jinshui's payments were made through Hao Yu Company's financial staff, and thus that apparent agency was not established, this argument is premised on a nature that is inconsistent with Hao Yu Company's sales conduct in this case being authorized agency. Furthermore, considering the specific process and circumstances of agency sales, advertising marketing, contract signing, and payment, Jinan Company's claim regarding the fault standard of the counterparty also exceeds the reasonable duty of care of Su Jinshui as an ordinary home buyer, and this Court does not support it. In summary, the agency acts performed by Hao Yu Company based on an effective principal-agent relationship do not violate prohibitive provisions of laws and regulations, and should be deemed valid. The legal consequences of its agency acts should directly bind the principal, and the resulting civil liability should be directly borne by the principal. Contracts No. 06 and No. 07 signed by Hao Yu Company as the entrusted agent should directly bind the principal, Jinan Company. The legal consequences of the payments collected by Hao Yu Company as the entrusted agent should also be attributed to the principal, Jinan Company. The corresponding civil liability arising from Hao Yu Company's actions should be borne by Jinan Company. Moreover, Hao Yu Company sold the involved shops to Su Jinshui in the name of the principal, Jinan Company, and not in its own name. A necessary prerequisite for establishing undisclosed agency is that the agent enters into a contract with a third party in its own name. Therefore, the second-instance judgment applied Article 402 of the Contract Law of the PRC to hold that Hao Yu Company's sale of Shop No. 07 constituted undisclosed agency. Although this does not affect the ultimate determination of the contract's validity, it constitutes an improper application of law, and this Court hereby corrects it.

2. The issue of whether Jinan Company bears corresponding compensation liability to Su Jinshui for separately selling Shop No. 06 and Shop No. 07.

According to Article 8 of this Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Commercial Housing Sales Contracts, "Under any of the following circumstances, causing the purpose of the commercial housing sales contract to be unattainable, the buyer who cannot obtain the house may request to rescind the contract, return the paid purchase price and interest, claim damages, and may also request the seller to bear compensation liability not exceeding the amount of the paid purchase price: (1) after the commercial housing sales contract is concluded, the seller mortgages the house to a third party without informing the buyer; (2) after the commercial housing sales contract is concluded, the seller sells the house to a third party." It is evident that as long as the seller actually sells the house to a third party after the conclusion of the commercial housing sales contract, the buyer who cannot obtain the house may request the seller to bear compensation liability not exceeding the amount of the paid purchase price. Moreover, the above provision does not require that the application of such compensation liability be premised on the seller having malicious intent to breach the contract. In April 2006, Hao Yu Company, as the entrusted agent, entered into Contract No. 06 and Contract No. 07 with Su Jinshui. In terms of legal consequences, this means that the principal, Jinan Company, had entered into Contract No. 06 and Contract No. 07 with Su Jinshui. Subsequently, Jinan Company sold the houses to a third party other than Su Jinshui, resulting in Su Jinshui's inability to obtain Shop No. 06 and Shop No. 07. Su Jinshui is entitled, under Article 8, paragraph 2 of this Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Commercial Housing Sales Contracts, to request Jinan Company to bear compensation liability not exceeding the amount of his paid purchase price. Jinan Company's related retrial requests effectively seek to improperly shift the business risks of its selection and supervision of the entrusted agent onto the buyer, and this Court does not support them. Under the circumstances where Jinan Company's separate sale of the shops rendered Contract No. 06 and Contract No. 07 impossible to perform, the second-instance court's judgment rescinding Contract No. 06 and Contract No. 07 based on Su Jinshui's claim was not improper. At the same time, the second-instance court, in its discretion, ordered Jinan Company to bear compensation liability to Su Jinshui in the amount of 50% of the purchase price. Su Jinshui, as the person entitled to dispose of the relevant rights, expressed in the retrial that he respects the second-instance judgment on this point. Therefore, this Court will not adjust this compensation ratio.

Additionally, 1. The issue of the scope of retrial review. Su Jinshui argued in the retrial that, since the procuratorate did not support Jinan Company's retrial requests, according to Article 33 of this Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC in the Trial Supervision Procedure, Jinan Company's arguments should not be included in the scope of retrial review. The basis for Su Jinshui's claim is his belief that the reasons for the procuratorate's protest differ from the reasons for Jinan Company's understanding of the validity of the two sales contracts. However, a party's litigation claims are different from the reasons and bases supporting their claims. The fact that Jinan Company's reasons and bases for its understanding of the contract validity differ from the reasons and bases put forth in the protest does not mean that its retrial requests were not supported by the protest. Moreover, Jinan Company's retrial requests did not exceed the scope of the original trial of this case. Therefore, this Court does not support Su Jinshui's argument. In the retrial, Su Jinshui also argued that the earlier decisions by the Wuhan Intermediate People's Court of Hubei Province to set aside the arbitration award in this case, the first-instance judgment, and the enforcement actions were all illegal. Since this Court's retrial of this case is based on the protest filed by the Supreme People's Procuratorate against the second-instance judgment of the Hubei High People's Court, the scope of its review is generally limited to the scope of the original trial. Su Jinshui's aforementioned arguments were not raised in the original trial and clearly fall outside the scope of retrial review. This Court will not address them. 2. The issue of whether the liability determined for Hao Yu Company in the second-instance judgment should be modified. Given that the conduct of the entrusted agent Hao Yu Company in selling Shop No. 06 and Shop No. 07 constituted authorized agency and Contract No. 06 and Contract No. 07 were rescinded, according to law, the principal, Jinan Company, should bear the sole obligation to return the purchase price and compensate for the loss of capital occupation to Su Jinshui. However, the second-instance court ordered Hao Yu Company to return the purchase price and compensate for the loss of capital occupation to Su Jinshui, with Jinan Company bearing supplementary compensation liability. This Court should have corrected this in accordance with the law. However, considering that modifying the judgment would increase the liability burden on the petitioner, Jinan Company, and that the second-instance court's determination of compensation liability neither exceeded the overall scope of Su Jinshui's claims nor substantively harmed Su Jinshui's interests, nor harmed national or public interests, and Su Jinshui did not object to it in the retrial, and Hao Yu Company, as a civil subject entitled to dispose of its own rights, also requested in the retrial to uphold the second-instance judgment, to respect the parties' right of disposition and maintain stable social relations and order that have already been established, this Court will not modify it.

In conclusion, in accordance with Article 207 and Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, this Court renders the following judgment:

Affirm the Civil Judgment No. 28 (2009) E-Min-Yi-Zhong of the Hubei High People's Court.

This judgment is final.
